skills.name: chow_ring_of_projective_space
skills.description: Express the Chow ring of a projective space as a polynomial algebra generated by the hyperplane class with the relation that its top power vanishes.
skills.preconditions: A projective space of any dimension is given.
skills.postconditions: A presentation of its Chow ring in terms of a single generator and a single vanishing relation is obtained.
skills.example: For the projective line, the Chow ring is generated by a class h with the relation that h squared is zero.

skills.name: product_chow_ring_via_kunneth
skills.description: Compute the Chow ring of a product of smooth varieties by taking the tensor product of the individual Chow rings and imposing commutativity of the classes.
skills.preconditions: The Chow rings of each factor are known.
skills.postconditions: A description of the Chow ring of the product as a graded tensor product is produced.
skills.example: For a product of two projective lines, the Chow ring is generated by two hyperplane classes h1 and h2 with the relations that each square is zero.

skills.name: intersection_product_using_chern_classes
skills.description: Translate an intersection condition into a Chern class computation and evaluate the degree via the top Chern class of the associated bundle.
skills.preconditions: A vector bundle whose zero locus represents the intersection is given.
skills.postconditions: The degree of the intersection cycle is expressed as the integral of the top Chern class.
skills.example: On a surface, intersecting two divisor classes can be computed by taking the product of their first Chern classes and integrating over the surface.

skills.name: apply_projection_formula
skills.description: Replace the pushforward of a product by the product of the pushforward and the class being pulled back when a proper morphism is involved.
skills.preconditions: A proper morphism between smooth varieties and Chow classes on the source are given.
skills.postconditions: An equality relating the pushforward of a product to a product of pushforwards is established.
skills.example: For the projection from a product of a curve and a projective space onto the curve, the pushforward of a class pulled back from the curve equals the class on the curve multiplied by the degree of the fiber.

skills.name: verify_finite_etale_by_jacobian_nonvanishing
skills.description: Check that the Jacobian matrix of a morphism has maximal rank at points of interest to conclude the map is finite étale over that locus.
skills.preconditions: A morphism between smooth varieties is given together with local coordinates.
skills.postconditions: The morphism is certified as finite étale on the specified open subset.
skills.example: A map defined by generic linear forms from affine space to affine space has a Jacobian with constant nonzero determinant, hence is finite étale.

skills.name: apply_frobenius_trace_to_point_counts
skills.description: Relate the number of rational points on a smooth proper variety over a finite field to the trace of Frobenius acting on its étale cohomology groups.
skills.preconditions: A smooth proper variety over a finite field is given.
skills.postconditions: An expression for the point count in terms of alternating sums of Frobenius traces on cohomology is obtained.
skills.example: For an elliptic curve over a finite field, the number of points equals the size of the field plus one minus the trace of Frobenius on the first cohomology.

skills.name: average_fiber_size_via_chebotarev_density
skills.description: Interpret the limiting average size of fibers of a finite étale cover as the proportion of Frobenius elements fixing a point, using Chebotarev density.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale cover of a geometrically connected base defined over a number field is given.
skills.postconditions: The average fiber cardinality over large finite fields is expressed as the density of the identity conjugacy class in the Galois group.
skills.example: For a quadratic cover of the projective line, the average number of points in a fiber over large finite fields approaches two times the density of Frobenius elements acting trivially.

skills.name: generic_smoothness_to_ensure_transversality
skills.description: Apply generic smoothness to guarantee that for a dense open set of parameters a family of subvarieties meets a given one transversely, yielding the expected dimension.
skills.preconditions: A morphism from a smooth parameter space to the space of subvarieties is given.
skills.postconditions: A dense open subset of parameters is identified where all intersections are transverse.
skills.example: A family of lines moving in the plane meets a fixed smooth curve transversely for a generic choice of line.

skills.name: use_bott_residue_for_equivariant_intersections
skills.description: Compute a global intersection number on a variety with torus action by localizing to its isolated fixed points via the Bott residue formula.
skills.preconditions: A torus action with isolated fixed points and an equivariant cohomology class are given.
skills.postconditions: The intersection number is expressed as a sum of contributions from each fixed point.
skills.example: On projective space with the standard diagonal torus action, the degree of a line bundle is obtained by summing the reciprocals of the weights at the coordinate fixed points.

skills.name: apply_inclusion_exclusion_to_tangent_conditions
skills.description: Separate overlapping tangency or incidence conditions by inclusion–exclusion, counting configurations satisfying each subset of conditions and alternating signs.
skills.preconditions: A collection of incidence conditions that may share solutions is given.
skills.postconditions: The total number of configurations satisfying all conditions is obtained by alternating sums of counts for subsets.
skills.example: Counting lines tangent to two distinct conics can be performed by adding the counts of lines tangent to each conic separately and subtracting the count of lines tangent to both.
